plain.text: Abraham married another wife, Keturah, and had more sons. He left everything he owned to Isaac, but gave gifts to his other sons and sent them away to the east.

Abraham lived 175 years. He died at a good old age, an old man full of years, and was gathered to his people. His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah with Sarah. After Abraham's death, God blessed his son Isaac.
This is the family line of Ishmael. He had twelve sons who became tribal rulers. Ishmael lived 137 years and died. His descendants settled to the east.

This is the family line of Isaac. Isaac was forty when he married Rebekah. She was childless, so Isaac prayed for her, and the LORD answered. She became pregnant with twins who struggled together inside her. The LORD told her, "Two nations are in your womb. One will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger." The first was born red and hairy, and they named him Esau. His brother came out grasping Esau's heel, so they named him Jacob. Esau became a skilful hunter, and Jacob stayed among the tents. Isaac loved Esau, who brought him wild game, but Rebekah loved Jacob.

One day Jacob was cooking stew when Esau came in from the open country, exhausted. "Quick, let me have some of that red stew!" Jacob said, "First sell me your birthright", the special rights of the firstborn son. Esau said, "I am about to die; what good is a birthright to me?" He swore an oath and sold his birthright to Jacob. Jacob gave him bread and lentil stew. Esau ate and drank, got up and left. So Esau despised his birthright.

summary.bigIdea: Abraham dies full of years, and the promise passes to Isaac, whose twin sons Jacob and Esau begin a long rivalry.
points: Abraham dies at a good old age; Isaac and Ishmael bury him together.
God says of Rebekah's twins, "The older will serve the younger."
Esau sells his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew.
summary.reflection: Esau traded something precious for a quick meal. What precious things might we be tempted to trade for something quick?
